FINANCIAL INDEBTEDNESS 
Our Company and our Subsidiaries avail certain credit facilities in their ordinary course of business, inter alia, for meeting their 
working capital, capital expenditure and other business requirements.  
 
Our Board is empowered to borrow monies, in accordance with Section 179 and Section 180 of the Companies Act and our 
Articles of Association. For details regarding the borrowing powers of our Company, please see “Our Management – Borrowing 
Powers” on page 291. 
 
As of July 15, 2026, the outstanding borrowings of our Company and our Subsidiaries (on a consolidated basis) aggregated to 
₹ 2,745.67 million (including non-fund based borrowings of ₹ 212.46 million). The details of such outstanding borrowings on 
a consolidated basis, are provided below:

Principal terms of the borrowings availed by our Company and our Subsidiaries:  
 
The details provided below are indicative and there may be additional terms, conditions and requirements under various loan 
documents executed by Company and our Subsidiaries in relation to our borrowings.  
 
1. Interest/Coupon Rate: The applicable rate of interest for the facilities availed by our Company and our Subsidiaries varies 
depending on the nature and type of facility. The working capital facilities availed by our Company carry interest rates 
ranging from 8.44% per annum to such other rates as may be mutually agreed with the relevant lender prior to limit loading 
or disbursement, with the lenders reserving the right to revise the applicable rate of interest from time to time.  
 
The term loan facilities carry interest linked to the one-year marginal cost of funds based lending rate plus a spread ranging 
from 2.75% per annum to 3.80% per annum or such other rate as may be mutually agreed with the relevant lender, subject 
to variation in the event  of drawals beyond the availability period or changes in market conditions. The fixed deposit 
overdraft facilities availed by our Company carry interest at a spread ranging from 0.50% to 0.75% per annum above the 
applicable fixed deposit rate. 
 
The fixed deposit overdraft facility availed by our Subsidiaries carries interest at 0.70% per annum above the applicable 
fixed deposit rate. 
 
2. Tenor: The working capital facilities availed by our Company are generally repayable on demand or on a revolving basis, 
with relevant sub-facilities carrying tenors ranging from 90 days per drawdown to 54 months depending on the nature of 
the sub -facility. The fixed deposit overdraft facilities availed by our Company are available for periods of 12 months, 
subject to renewal and the maturity of the underlying fixed deposits. The term loan facilities availed by our Company carry 
tenors ranging from eight months to approximately seven years, with certain longer-dated term loans inclusive of applicable 
moratorium periods of up to 1 year from the date of the first disbursement  or scheduled commercial operation date . The 
fixed deposit overdraft facility availed by our Subsidiaries carries a tenor of 12 months  and is renewable upon expiry. 
 
3. Repayment: The working capital facilities and fixed deposit overdraft facilities availed by our Company and our 
Subsidiaries are generally repayable on demand or upon maturity of the underlying fixed deposits  or prior to the expiry 
date as specified in the relevant loan documentation . The term loan facilities are repayable in equal quarterly instalments 
as per the repayment schedules stipulated in the relevant loan documentation, following the applicable moratorium periods. 
  
4. Penal interest : The borrowings availed include provisions for, inter alia , levy of penal interest, over and above the 
prescribed interest rate, for delayed payment or default in the repayment obligations by our Company and Subsidiaries. 
Such penal interest can range from 1.00% to up to 2.0 0% per month (excluding applicable taxes)  over and above the

applicable interest rate/ coupon rate. 
 
5. Pre-payment penalty: The borrowings availed typically include pre-payment provisions which allow for pre -payment of 
the outstanding amount with the prepayment charges ranging up to 2.00% or as may be determined by the lender , subject 
to the conditions specified in the loan documents.  
 
6. Security: The working capital and term loan facilities are secured by way of first, pari passu  charges by way of 
hypothecation over the current assets and moveable fixed assets of our Company. Certain facilities are further secured by 
way of lien marked fixed deposits and exclusive cash margin charges in favour of the relevant lenders.  
 
7. Restrictive Covenants: Our Company and Subsidiaries are required to comply with various financial covenants, restrictive 
covenants and conditions restricting certain corporate actions, and our Company and our Subsidiaries  are required to take 
prior written consent from the lender and/or intimate the respective lender before carrying out such actions, including, but 
not limited to the following: 
 
a. to effect any adverse changes in our capital structure; 
b. to formulate or effect any scheme of amalgamation or merger or reconstitution; 
c. to undertake any activity other than the activities indicated in the objects clause of the memorandum of association of 
our Company and our Subsidiaries; 
d. for any transfer of the controlling interest or the management set up of our Company  and our Subsidiaries; 
e. for declaring any dividend or distribution of profits, if any instalment towards principal or interest remains unpaid on 
its due date;  
f. to make any investments, including by way of loans or investments in share capital or otherwise in any of our 
subsidiaries; and 
g. to create encumbrance, lien or dispose of assets charged in favour of the lenders.  
 
8. Events of default: Our borrowing arrangements contain standard events of default including, among others:  
 
a. non-payment of money on due date or on demand; 
b. breach of or default in the performance of or observance of any of the terms, covenants, obligations or undertakings 
stipulated in the loan documents; 
c. incorrect or misleading representations, warranties or statements under the loan documents; 
d. failure to get any charge or security registered in accordance with applicable law;  
e. appointment of a receiver or any attachment, distress, execution or other legal process being levied or enforced against 
our Company or our Subsidiaries or their respective assets; 
f. occurrence of event or circumstance which could have a material adverse effect on the lender;  
g. utilization of any facility or any part thereof for any purpose other than that for which it was sanctioned; and  
h. cross default in respect of any borrowings of our Company or Subsidiaries. 
 
9. Consequences of occurrence of events of default: In terms of our borrowing arrangements for the facilities availed, the 
following, among others, are the consequences of occurrence of events of default, whereby our lenders may: 
 
a. accelerate repayment of facilities or declare all sums outstanding as immediately due and payable;  
b. enforce their security interest over the hypothecated, charged or lien-marked assets; 
c. exercise, initiate and pursue any action, rights, notices, remedies or proceedings (including litigation), whether civil, 
criminal or otherwise, against our Company or our Subsidiaries, their assets and properties, whether simultaneously 
or separately, jointly or severally; 
d. without notice to or consent from our Company or our Subsidiaries, appoint any receiver, agent, manager or other 
person to exercise all or any of the powers and rights vested in the relevant lender under the loan documents; 
e. report and disclose information to the Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited / information utility and / or any 
other agency so authorised by RBI as may be required under applicable law; and  
f. appoint nominee directors; and 
g. at the option of the relevant lender, convert the whole or part of the outstanding amounts into equity shares of our 
Company at face value and/or formulate a mechanism for resolution of the stressed asset. 
 
We have obtained the necessary consent s and waivers, as applicable  from our lenders as  required under the relevant loan 
documents for undertaking activities in relation to the Offer. For risks in relation to the financial and other covenants required 
to be complied with in relation to our borrowings, refer “ Risk Factors – We have breached certain financial covenants under 
our financing arrangements in the past, which have been waived by the relevant lenders. Our inability to meet our obligations, 
including financial and other restrictive covenants, under our debt financing arrangements could adversely affect our business, 
results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows.” on page 30.

MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF 
OPERATIONS 
 
You should read the following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations, in conjunction with our Restated 
Consolidated Summary Statements included in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus as of and for the Financial Years 2026, 2025 
and 2024, including the related notes, schedules and annexures. This discussion contains certain forward -looking statements 
that involve risks and uncertainties and reflect our current view with respect to future events and financial performance, ma ny 
of which are beyond our control, which may cause the actual results to be different from those expressed or implied by the 
forward-looking statements. You should read “Forward -Looking Statements” on page 25 for a discussion of the risks and 
uncertainties related to those statements and also “Risk Factors” on page 26 for a discussion of certain risks that may affect 
our business, financial condition and results of operations.  
 
We have included certain non-Ind AS financial measures and other performance metrics relating to our financial performance 
and business in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, each of which is a supplemental measure of our performance and liquidity 
and not required by, or presented in accordance with, Ind AS, IFRS or U.S. GAAP. Furthermore, such measures and metrics 
are not defined under Ind AS, IFRS, U.S. GAAP or other accounting standards, and therefore should not be viewed as substitutes 
for performance, liquidity, or profitability measures under such accounting standards. In addition, such measures and metrics 
are not standardized terms and a direct comparison of these measures and metrics between companies may not be possible. 
Other companies may calculat e these measures and metrics differently from us, limiting their usefulness as a comparative 
measure. Although such measures and metrics are not a measure of performance calculated in accordance with applicable 
accounting standards, our management believes  that they are useful to an investor in evaluating our operating performance. 
Also see “Risk Factors – We have included in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus certain non -generally accepted accounting 
principle financial measures and certain other selected statistical information related to our operations and financial condition. 
These non-GAAP financial measures are not measures of operating performance or liquidity defined by Ind AS and may not be 
comparable with those presented by other companies ” and “Risk Factors – Significant differences exist between Indian 
Accounting Standards and other accounting principles, such as Indian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, U.S. 
Generally Accepted Accounting Principles and International Financial Reporting Stan dards, which may be relevant to 
investors’ assessment of our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows”  on pages 61 and 63, respectively. 
 
Unless otherwise indicated, the industry and market -related information contained in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus is 
derived from the report titled “Next-Generation Consumer Appliances & Proprietary Motors Industry Report ” dated August 
19, 2026 (the “Redseer Report”), which has been commissioned and paid for by our Company for an agreed fee for the purposes 
of confirming our understanding of the industry exclusively in connection with the Offer. We officially engaged Redseer Strategy 
Consultants Private Limited in connection with the preparation of the Redseer Report pursuant to an engagement letter dated 
March 25, 2026 . The Redseer Report will be avail able on the website of our Company at www.atomberg.com/investors until 
the Bid/Offer Closing Date and will also form part of the material documents for inspection, as set out in “Material Contract s 
and Documents for Inspection – Material Documents” on page 484. The information included in this section includes excerpts 
from the Redseer Report and may have been reordered by us for the purposes of presentation. There are no parts, data or 
information (which may be relevant for the Offer), that have been left out or changed in any manner. Also see “Risk Factors – 
This Draft Red Herring Prospectus contains information from third parties, including an industry report prepared by an 
independent third -party research agency, which we have commissioned and paid for t o confirm our understanding of our 
industry exclusively in connection with the Offer and reliance on such information for making an investment decision in the 
Offer is subject to inherent risks” on page 60.

proprietary, internally developed technologies embedded within the core product architecture and manufacturing processes, spanning domains

capabilities are driving the adoption of next-generation consumer appliances in India” on page 182.
